name: Boeing 777-200
sources: [777] Boeing D6-58329 Rev E (December 2024), 777-200/-200ER/-300 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/acaps/777-200-200ER-300_Rev_E.pdf. 777-200 (fig 2.2.1, p.2-8; the 777-200ER has no drawing of its own): overall length 63.73 m (209 ft 1 in), fuselage 62.94 m (206 ft 6 in), span 60.93 m (199 ft 11 in), wing root 21.58 m (70 ft 9.5 in) aft of the nose, engine inlet 20.13 m (Trent, 66 ft 0.5 in), 20.22 m (PW, 66 ft 4 in) and 20.42 m (GE, 67 ft 0 in), wingtip 39.94 m (131 ft 0 in) and 42.06 m (138 ft 0 in), nose gear 5.89 m (19 ft 4 in) aft of the nose, wheelbase 25.88 m (84 ft 11 in), track 10.97 m. 777-300 (fig 2.2.2, p.2-9): overall length 73.86 m (242 ft 4 in), fuselage 73.08 m (239 ft 9 in), span 60.93 m, wing root 26.89 m (88 ft 2.5 in), engine inlet 25.47 m (Trent, 83 ft 6.5 in), 83 ft 10 in (PW) and 84 ft 6 in (GE; the drawing's metres for these two, 25.66 and 27.62, do not match its feet), wingtip 45.26 m (148 ft 6 in) and 47.40 m (155 ft 6 in), nose gear 5.89 m, wheelbase 31.22 m (102 ft 5 in), track 10.97 m.

Fuselage [777]: the 777-300 is the 777-200 with two body sections added to the fuselage (section 1.3, p.1-2). The 777-200 is 10.13 m (33 ft 3 in) shorter, overall and in the fuselage alone. The document prints no plug lengths; they come from the holds and the stations. Ahead of the wing, 17 ft 6 in (5.33 m): the forward hold is 14.96 m (49 ft 1 in) against 20.30 m (66 ft 7 in) (fig 2.6.1, p.2-20); the nose gear stays 5.89 m from the nose, and the wheelbase (102 ft 5.3 in to 84 ft 11.1 in, section 7.2, p.7-5), the three engine inlets and the two wingtip stations are each 17 ft 6 in nearer the nose; the wing root gives 17 ft 5 in (5.31 m). Behind the wing, 15 ft 9 in (4.80 m): the aft hold is 11.36 m (37 ft 3 in) against 16.16 m (53 ft 0 in); the bulk hold is 4.47 m on both (fig 2.6.1). The first door behind the wing is 36.33 m (119 ft 2 in) from the nose against 46.46 m (152 ft 5 in), and the last door 49.54 m (162 ft 6 in) against 59.66 m (195 ft 9 in): each 33 ft 3 in less (fig 2.7.1, p.2-23), so both lengths come out ahead of the first door behind the wing. -5.33 - 4.80 = -10.13 m = 63.73 - 73.86 m: no rest.

Doors [777] fig 2.7.1, p.2-23, centre lines from the nose. 777-200: four doors on each side, 6.75 m (22 ft 1.5 in), 17.07 m (56 ft), 36.33 m (119 ft 2 in), 49.54 m (162 ft 6 in). 777-300: five, 6.75 m, 17.07 m, 32.92 m (108 ft), 46.46 m, 59.66 m. Doors 1 and 2 do not move. The 777-300's door 3, over the wing, is the pair that the 777-200 does not have: the recipe has stations of its own. Cockpit side windows: the same nose as the base, aft edge 2.98 m from the nose (2.98 m off the 777-200 drawing of fig 2.7.1, scaled by its door 1 and door 2 stations).

The same on both aircraft, so the recipe has no wingtip, nacelle or gear. Wing [777]: span 60.93 m and the same plain tip (fig 2.2.1, 2.2.2). Nacelles: the same three engine families, GE90, PW4000 and Trent 800 (section 1.3, p.1-3); axis 9.61 m (31 ft 6.5 in) from the centre line on both; nacelle ground clearance 0.96 to 1.04 m (PW), 0.85 to 0.93 m (GE), 1.09 to 1.17 m (RR) on both (tables 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, p.2-10, 2-11). Gear, section 7.2, p.7-5: six wheels on each main leg and two on the nose leg, one footprint for the 777-200, -200ER and -300 (track 10.97 m, main wheels 1.40 m apart, axles 1.45 m apart, nose wheels 0.78 m apart), main tyres 50x20.0R22 and nose tyres 42x17.0R18 on all three. Only the wheelbase differs: 25.88 m against 31.22 m.

B77L (777-200LR and 777 Freighter), drawn on this model: [LR] Boeing D6-58329-2 Rev G (December 2024), 777-200LR/-300ER/-Freighter Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning, https://www.boeing.com/content/dam/boeing/v2/airports/acaps/777-200LR-300ER-F_Rev_G.pdf. The 777-200LR has the fuselage of the 777-200/-200ER (section 1.3, p.1-2), and the freighter is based on it (p.1-3): overall length 63.73 m, fuselage 62.94 m, wing root 21.58 m, nose gear 5.89 m, wheelbase 25.89 m (fig 2.2.1, p.2-3; fig 2.2.3, p.2-5); the 777-200LR's doors 6.74, 17.07, 36.32 and 49.53 m (fig 2.7.1, p.2-19). They differ from this model: raked wingtips, span 64.80 m (212 ft 7 in); GE90-110B and -115B engines only (p.1-3); main tyres 52x21.0R22, nose tyres 43x17.5R17 (section 7.2, p.7-5); the freighter has one door on each side (6.74 m) and no cabin windows. This model shows them with the 777-200ER's wing, nacelles and doors.
